items.title: General Motors (GM) Stock May Trade At A Premium Despite Its 171% Run
items.summary: General Motors stock has delivered a 170.8% return over the past three years, yet its valuation sends mixed signals. A Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) intrinsic value estimate indicates the shares trade at a 37.1% discount, while market multiples screen the stock as overvalued. A 170.8% gain over three years puts General Motors among the stronger performers in large-cap autos. This raises the bar for what counts as a reasonable entry price today. items.title: 1 Value Stock with Impressive Fundamentals and 2 We Find Risky
items.summary: Value stocks typically trade at discounts to the broader market, offering patient investors the opportunity to buy businesses when they’re out of favor. The key risk, however, is that these stocks are usually cheap for a reason, and a low valuation can reflect underlying business challenges rather than a genuine bargain.

items.title: Fresh Tariffs Boost Domestic Steel, Dent Automakers
items.summary: Trade talks between the U.S. and Canada collapsed in the 11th hour Friday, renewing fears of an all-out trade war as new tariffs went into effect over the weekend. Ford and Stellantis shares slipped Monday after President Trump announced a 50% tariff on automobiles and auto parts from Canada come January.

items.title: U.S. and Canada Escalate Their Trade Fight. It Won’t Be the Last Tariff Tiff.
items.summary: Another trade war has started with a volley of tariff threats, and this time the fight is with America’s neighbor and closest trading partner, Canada.  While the U.S. has held several formal negotiations with Mexico this year about the USMCA, it hasn’t done so with Canada.
